The family’s complaint says Janene was tossing material onto her own property, away from the neighbor, and quotes Blackburn acknowledging that the video captured no suspect, only describing thuds nearby.

The officers entered without a warrant and with no apparent emergency justifying entry. According to the lawsuit, when Janene’s husband, Christopher, tried to end the conversation and close the door, Craig blocked it with his foot, then forced it open and entered, followed by Blackburn. The lawsuit states that Craig grabbed Janene and dragged her toward the doorway. Their lawsuit challenges the entry, use of force, and the department’s handling of the underlying neighbor dispute.

sections.title: Lawsuit
descriptions: Janene Thorpe and members of her family filed a federal civil-rights lawsuit in April 2023 against American Fork City, Cedar Hills City, several AFPD officers, and others. The lawsuit was ongoing as of September 2026.

segments.text: The filing history for the federal lawsuit through September 28, 2026. The latest entries show that motions involving discovery, expert testimony, and summary judgment were still being addressed.

The Thorpe plaintiffs allege federal civil-rights violations and related state-law claims involving American Fork City, Cedar Hills City, AFPD, and several officers. These are allegations, not court findings.
The basic filing information submitted when the federal lawsuit was opened.
A parcel map filed with the complaint to show the properties involved in the underlying dispute.

sections.title: Civil Background
descriptions: Records from three separate Utah civil proceedings involving Janene Thorpe and the Sanches family. These provide background on the underlying neighbor disputes and are separate from the federal civil-rights lawsuit.
